# Project overview

This reproducible research project evaluates genomic prediction with a
GBLUP-ADE genomic mixed model and artificial neural networks with no
regularization, L1 regularization, L2 regularization, or simultaneous L1+L2
regularization.

The analytical design contains two complementary branches: controlled
simulated genomic data and real longitudinal *Coffea arabica* data.

## Scientific question

The central question is whether neural-network weight regularization improves
predictive performance and generalization relative to an unregularized ANN and
a genomic mixed-model benchmark when all competing methods are evaluated under
a common validation design.

For simulated data, known true genetic values provide an independent target
for predictive assessment.

For real data, repeated field observations are first analyzed with a
phenotypic mixed model. Individual genotypic BLUPs from that model become the
phenotypic targets for the genomic-prediction workflow.

## Simulated-data workflow

```text
simulated_data_audit.Rmd
        |
        v
simulated_data_validation.Rmd
        |
        +-------------------+
        |                   |
        v                   v
simulated_data_gblup.Rmd   simulated_data_ann.Rmd
        |                   |
        +---------+---------+
                  |
                  v
      simulated_data_comparison.Rmd
```

## Real-data workflow

```text
real_data_phenotype.Rmd
        |
        v
real_data_audit.Rmd
        |
        v
real_data_validation.Rmd
        |
        +-------------------+
        |                   |
        v                   v
real_data_gblup.Rmd       real_data_ann.Rmd
        |                   |
        +---------+---------+
                  |
                  v
        real_data_comparison.Rmd
```

The real-data workflow begins with the complete longitudinal phenotypic
dataset. `real_data_phenotype.Rmd` performs descriptive analysis, organizes the
experimental data, fits the phenotypic mixed model with `sommer`, and obtains
individual genotypic BLUPs.

`real_data_audit.Rmd` then integrates those BLUPs with `geno_real.rds`, aligns
the common individuals, performs genotype quality control, and creates the
common object consumed by the remaining real-data modules.

Validation design, GBLUP-ADE fitting, ANN fitting, and terminal comparison are
kept in separate pages.

## Models

Five genomic-prediction configurations are compared:

- GBLUP-ADE;
- ANN without L1/L2 regularization;
- ANN-L1;
- ANN-L2;
- ANN-L1+L2.

All competing models use the same outer-assessment partitions within each
dataset and task.

## Validation principles

The analytical design separates model development from final predictive
assessment.

Outer-assessment responses do not enter model fitting, ANN hyperparameter
selection, or ANN epoch selection. Competing methods are evaluated on matched
held-out individuals using the same task definitions and predictive metrics.

For the simulated branch, true genetic values are excluded from model fitting
and model selection and are used as an independent evaluation target.

## Reproducibility

The project is organized with `workflowr`. Source analyses are stored under
`analysis/`, derived analytical objects under `output/`, and the rendered site
under `docs/`.

Project-level R package versions are recorded in `renv.lock`.
